reference_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t
WHERE t.n_orders > (
  SELECT AVG(t2.n_orders)
  FROM (
    -- one row per registered customer
    SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) AS t2
)

  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM customer_orders
WHERE n_orders > (SELECT AVG(n_orders) FROM customer_orders)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers
FROM (
  -- one row per registered customer
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
) AS t
WHERE t.n_orders > (
  SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_customers FROM t WHERE n_orders > (SELECT AVG(n_orders) FROM t)
